article.title: Stock markets decline in early trade amid rising crude oil prices
article.text: Indian stock market indices declined in early trading as crude oil prices rose. From the Sensex pack, Bharti Airtel, Mahindra & Mahindra, UltraTech Cement, Adani Ports, Titan and Bajaj Finance were among the major laggards.
article.note: Recorded replay of the real article-4334 production run (newsflo-local llm_stage_cache, 2026-08-14) -- a headline about a broad market decline that names ONLY the article's own laggards (none of them crude-linked beneficiaries or crude-cost payers), while the extracted facts separately establish a crude-price-up event. Every crude-linked candidate below is discovered through the knowledge-registry archetype chain (broad path), never through the named laggards -- this is what makes the correct verdict 'governed secondary_ripple breadth, zero primary': no company is the article's own subject, so ARTICLE_SUBJECT/SUBJECT evidence never applies here.

universe.business_desc: Small onshore and offshore oil and gas exploration and production company with a gas-weighted production mix.

universe.business_desc: India's largest airline by market share, operating a single-fleet low-cost air transport network where aviation turbine fuel is the dominant operating cost.

universe.name: SpiceJet
universe.business_desc: Low-cost Indian airline with a financially stretched balance sheet and limited fuel hedging capacity.

universe.name: Blue Dart Express
universe.business_desc: Air transport and ground logistics operator running dedicated airline freighters alongside a road delivery fleet, with a contractual fuel surcharge pass-through mechanism to shippers.

universe.name: Indian Oil Corporation
universe.business_desc: India's largest downstream oil marketing company with the widest retail fuel network; administered pump pricing makes marketing margin the dominant earnings driver.

universe.name: Bharat Petroleum Corporation
universe.business_desc: Integrated refining and fuel marketing company with a large retail pump network subject to administered pricing lags.

universe.name: Hindustan Petroleum Corporation
universe.business_desc: Refining and marketing company with the highest marketing-to-refining ratio among the state oil marketing companies.

universe.name: Reliance Industries
universe.business_desc: Diversified export-oriented refining and petrochemicals conglomerate selling refined products at market-linked prices with no administered retail-pricing drag on its O2C segment.

universe.name: Castrol India
universe.business_desc: Branded automotive and industrial lubricant marketer whose principal raw material is crude-derived base oil, sold under a premium brand with real but lagged pricing power.

universe.name: Southern Petrochemicals Lubricants
universe.business_desc: Small petroleum-specialty and lubricant blender buying crude-derived base oil, with weaker brand pricing power than the premium lubricant marketers.

universe.name: Supreme Petrochem
universe.business_desc: Petrochemical polystyrene producer whose styrene and benzene feedstock costs are set by regional aromatics supply-demand and naphtha spreads.

universe.name: Tamilnadu Petroproducts
universe.business_desc: Small commodity petrochemical intermediates producer (LAB, epichlorohydrin) with crude/kerosene-derived feedstock and limited pricing power.

shocks.label: Crude oil price rises
shocks.mechanism: Crude oil benchmark prices move higher. Higher crude directly raises the landed cost of the marginal barrel for a net crude-importing economy like India, resetting the price of the single largest imported input in the economy.
evidence: Article states crude oil prices have risen
Market decline explicitly attributed to rising crude in the headline

shocks.label: Equity risk premium rises / broad-based index de-rating
shocks.mechanism: Higher crude raises expected inflation and import-bill uncertainty for an oil-importing economy, so discount rates and required risk premia rise while earnings estimates are marked down -- multiple compression across index heavyweights irrespective of direct oil exposure, which is what an early-trade broad decline reflects.
evidence: Stock market indices declined in early trading
Laggards span telecom, autos, cement, ports, discretionary retail and NBFC -- a broad de-rating rather than a single-sector move

direct_nodes.child_label: Broad equity valuation multiples / index level
direct_nodes.mechanism: Higher crude raises expected inflation and macro uncertainty, so the required equity risk premium rises and earnings estimates are trimmed, producing index-level multiple compression that hits large-cap heavyweights across unrelated sectors simultaneously -- what the broad early-trade decline expresses.

companies.mechanism: Higher crude price lifts per-barrel realization on domestic nomination-block output, boosting revenue and margin.
companies.rationale: India's largest crude producer; realization gains flow near fully to EBITDA, though subsidy/windfall-levy risk caps upside if prices spike further.
negative_channels: windfall cess risk if prices rise sharply

companies.mechanism: Crude realization per barrel rises on domestic production, directly expanding upstream revenue and operating margin.
companies.rationale: Pure-play upstream producer with high operating leverage to crude realizations; downstream refining subsidiary adds modest offsetting cost exposure.

companies.mechanism: Small upstream producer's crude realizations rise with benchmark prices, improving revenue per barrel.
companies.rationale: Genuine producing E&P with crude-linked realizations, but small output base and gas-weighted mix limit absolute earnings impact.

companies.mechanism: Higher crude lifts ATF prices; fuel is the largest single cost line for an airline, compressing operating margin.
companies.rationale: Largest domestic carrier; fuel-cost pass-through lags fares in a competitive low-cost market, so near-term margin compression.
positive_channels: strong domestic demand allows partial fare hikes

companies.mechanism: ATF cost rises with crude; thin liquidity and a weak balance sheet magnify the margin and cash strain.
companies.rationale: Financially stretched carrier with limited pricing power and cash buffers, so fuel inflation hits earnings and liquidity harder.
positive_channels: industry-wide fare increases if capacity tightens

companies.mechanism: Higher ATF and diesel raise air-express and ground fleet costs ahead of fuel-surcharge resets.
companies.rationale: Operates dedicated air-express freighters plus a road fleet; fuel surcharge mechanism recovers costs with a lag, so temporary margin drag.
positive_channels: contractual fuel surcharge pass-through to shippers

companies.mechanism: Higher crude raises fuel-purchase cost; retail pump prices held flat, compressing auto-fuel marketing margins.
companies.rationale: Largest domestic retail fuel network makes marketing margin dominant over GRM gains and inventory gains from rising crude.
negative_channels: marketing margin squeeze on capped retail pricing
higher working capital and interest cost

companies.mechanism: Crude cost up with administered retail prices sticky, narrowing petrol/diesel marketing margins.
companies.rationale: Marketing-weighted earnings mean pass-through lag outweighs modest refining spread and inventory benefits.

companies.mechanism: Rising crude lifts input cost while capped pump prices squeeze marketing margins; refining capacity is the smallest of the OMCs.
companies.rationale: Highest marketing-to-refining ratio among OMCs makes it most sensitive to pass-through lag on rising crude.

companies.mechanism: Export-oriented refining realizes market-linked product prices; petrochemical naphtha feedstock cost rises at the same time.
companies.rationale: No administered-price drag; gains from crude-linked realizations and inventory are offset by weaker petrochemical spreads.

companies.mechanism: Crude-linked base oil is the dominant lubricant input; costs rise before retail price hikes land.
companies.rationale: Branded lubricant pricing power softens the hit, but margin compression lags in the interim quarter.

companies.mechanism: Petroleum-specialty and lubricant maker buys crude-derived base oil; input cost up, thinner pass-through ability.
companies.rationale: Smaller, less brand-insulated player faces a sharper margin squeeze than premium lubricant marketers on base-oil inflation.
positive_channels: inventory gains on held stock if prices spike

companies.mechanism: Crude-linked styrene/benzene feedstock costs rise; polystyrene spreads compress on lagged pass-through.
companies.rationale: Pure crude-derived styrenics producer; margins track the styrene-minus-polystyrene delta, which narrows when feedstock rises faster than prices.
positive_channels: inventory revaluation gains on existing stock

companies.mechanism: Petrochemical intermediates (LAB, epichlorohydrin) use crude/kerosene-derived inputs; input costs rise, spreads narrow.
companies.rationale: Small commodity petrochemical producer with crude-derived feedstock and limited pricing power; margin compression likely if crude sustains higher.
positive_channels: possible price increases on downstream products

reject.reason: Micro-cap explorer with negligible commercial crude output; realization-uplift mechanism is not material at the corporate level and inclusion rests mainly on sector/name similarity to upstream producers. Effect too immaterial for a professional impact graph on an unquantified crude move.

Fuel is a modest, largely pass-through cost (fuel surcharge mechanism) for an express logistics operator; the incremental margin effect from an unquantified crude uptick is generic operating-cost noise rather than a material, event-specific impact.

Base-oil cost link is plausible but the exposure claim is generic small-cap specialty-lubricant reasoning; magnitude/pass-through ability is unverified and the effect from an unquantified crude move is too small and speculative to display alongside the primary base-oil name.

Styrene/benzene pricing is driven primarily by regional aromatics supply-demand and naphtha spreads rather than mechanically by a crude benchmark uptick; the crude -> styrene -> polystyrene spread chain requires an unsupported intermediate assumption and the effect is a niche downstream branch of a generic crude move.

Niche petrochemical intermediates producer; the crude -> kerosene/LAB feedstock -> spread compression chain depends on unsupported assumptions about contract pricing and is a tertiary input relationship that a generic crude move does not make central.

ground_truth.rationale: Recorded replay of the real article-4334 production run. The headline names ONLY the article's own laggards (Bharti Airtel, M&M, UltraTech, Adani Ports, Titan, Bajaj Finance) -- none of the nine crude-linked companies below is the article's own subject, so ARTICLE_SUBJECT/SUBJECT evidence never applies to any of them. Every one of them is discovered through the crude-price-shock knowledge-registry archetype chain at causal distance 2 with CURATED_ARCHETYPE/tier-D evidence, which caps them at secondary_ripple regardless of materiality grade -- tier D can never authorize primary (blueprint §3's ONGC example). The correct verdict is governed analytical breadth with ZERO primary claims: a real, valid, well-evidenced set of second-order companies that must never be mistaken for the article's own subjects. Five borderline/off-mechanism candidates (a micro-cap explorer, a logistics operator with a pass-through fuel surcharge, an under-brand-insulated lubricant blender and two niche petrochemical intermediates producers) are correctly rejected by the verifier for immateriality or an unsupported mechanism chain.
